summary: The paper sets out the dependence theory behind PFC, a translator that rewrites FORTRAN DO loops as FORTRAN 8x array statements. It gives a dependence test for linear subscripts, a code generator driven by the dependence graph, and loop interchange, recurrence breaking, threshold and IF-conversion transformations that expose more parallelism.
why_read: Read it for the dependence test and loop transformations that decide which FORTRAN loops can become vector statements.
main_contribution: A dependence-based code generator, built on a carrier-level test for linear subscripts, that emits array statements and adds loop interchange, recurrence breaking, thresholds and IF conversion.
main_limitation: Its dependence conditions are only necessary, so for linear subscripts the translator sometimes assumes a dependence that does not exist, and unknown symbolic constants force the same conservative assumption.
evaluation_method: proofs and worked examples, plus one translation-time comparison with PARAFRASE on a composite set of Los Alamos kernels
benchmarks: composite set of Los Alamos kernels (translation CPU time only)
states_relationship_to: Kuck et al. Illinois dependence work
Allen, Kennedy, Porterfield and Warren (IF conversion)
notes: Title differs only in capitalisation (catalog: 'Automatic translation of FORTRAN programs to vector form'). First author (Randy Allen) and year (1987) match the title page and journal line.
